context:
Goal: a lane can push its own rebased branch without being refused.
Problem (rule): the lease line you granted on #1307 covers only `--force-with-lease=<branch>:<sha>`. Most past refusals used the form with no sha, so they would still be refused.
Based on (read): the 9 refused lease pushes in docs/debts/notes.md, Nov 2-4.
Based on (ruling): your lease line on #1307 (item 262), now in draft PR #1316.
Departs from: #1316's line — option a also covers `--force-with-lease` with no sha on the session's own non-default branch. Option b keeps the line and adds a step: the lane brief and the refusal message name the sha form.

options.gain: The strictest lease. A session can always name the commit it expects, so it changes to fit the line.
options.how: The line stays as you granted it. The lane brief and the refusal message both show `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<sha>`.
options.label: Keep the sha form; teach it
options.lose: Lanes that use the old form get one refusal before they learn the right one.

options.gain: The rebase refusals stop with no change in habit.
options.how: The line also covers `--force-with-lease` with no sha, on the session's own branch only.
options.label: Also allow the no-sha form
options.lose: A lease with no sha only guards against what the session's last fetch saw, so it can overwrite a newer push.

reply: Moved off the page (your 316 note): tracked in PR #1316.
title: Should a lane's own-branch force push have to name the commit it expects?
why: A session can always name the commit, so it should fit the line, not the other way round.
